items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is readable, but the error message is misleading. Prefetch.__init__ filters nothing, yet it raises "Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken." The nested if restructuring is clean.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It adds a new guard in query.py instead of a shared helper in related_descriptors.py, which works against the needed fix. It also copies the filter() error text, so the same message now lives in two places. No reuse of ORM building blocks.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It turns a later failure into an earlier ValueError, so a feature the issue asks for is now blocked at construction time. That removes functionality instead of handling the case. The hidden tests fail: 0 of 4 fail-to-pass tests pass.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: There are no per-parent slice semantics at all. `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError(...)` rejects every sliced Prefetch queryset. There is no Window/RowNumber partitioning and no handling of high_mark. The PrefetchLimitTests fail.
